content: Sodium dichloroisocyanurate is a chemically stable compound that serves as a source of chlorine. It is widely utilized as a disinfectant, biocide, industrial deodorant, and detergent. In small quantities, it is commonly found in water purification tablets and filters. This compound is the sodium salt of dichloroisocyanuric acid. Products containing sodium dichloroisocyanurate may also include cyanuric acid as a component. It is typically white in color and is available in the form of crystallized granules, powder, or tablets. Structurally, it is a heterocyclic ring compound derived from triazine. Sodium dichloroisocyanurate is chemically reactive with water, urea, ammonia, reducing agents, and strong bases. When it reacts, it can release toxic fumes, including chlorine gas, which poses significant health and safety risks. Protective gloves and clothing should also be worn to minimize direct contact. If ingested, the affected individual should rest, rinse their mouth with water, and seek medical attention promptly. Vomiting should not be induced under any circumstances. In the event of a fire, containers or drums containing this substance may be cooled with water spray, but care must be taken to prevent the chemical from coming into direct contact with water. In case of spills, the substance should not be washed into public sewage systems to avoid contamination.
